glossary.definition: A large language model is an AI system trained on huge amounts of text so it gets very good at predicting what word should come next in a sentence. Think of it like the autocomplete on your phone keyboard, but instead of guessing one word from a few you typed, it has read a giant slice of the internet and can guess entire paragraphs, essays, or answers. That one trick, done at massive scale, is what lets it write, summarize, translate, and hold a conversation. ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all built on top of an LLM.

items.title: Google debuts flagship Gemini 4 Carbon model with cybersecurity upgrades
items.summary: Google LLC today debuted Gemini 4 Carbon, a frontier large language model adept at complex programming tasks. The LLM is rolling out just two weeks after the search introduced its previous flagship LLM, Gemini 4 Argon. According to Google, internal tests have shown Carbon to be more than twice as good at generating secure code. Additionally, the model outperforms GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 across multiple benchmarks.

items.title: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’
items.summary: Asked about AI and the trend of college students booing tech CEOs at graduation ceremonies, Instagram head Adam Mosseri acknowledged in an interview that a lot of people really don't like AI, and it's not just young people and creatives. Appearing on the Colin and Samir podcast to talk about the launch of widescreen and long-form video for Instagram , Mosseri said he thinks there's a trend of "more anxiety and more frustration and more anger about AI," particularly in creative industries: It's not only getting worse, it's going to continue to get worse. ’ It’s not only getting worse, it’s going to continue to get worse. I think we’re going to see more frustration and anger, some of it founded, some of it unfounded, over the next couple of years, and that’s going to make it hard for a lot of people, not just in the industry.

items.title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows
items.summary: The announcement came alongside parent company Alphabet's third-quarter earnings report, which saw revenue grow 25% year over year to $127.6 billion. Google is bringing ads in its AI-powered Search experiences to international markets, betting that generative AI can open up new revenue opportunities even as growth in its core search advertising business slows. The announcement came Wednesday during Alphabet’s third-quarter earnings call, as the company reported $127.6 billion in revenue, up 25% year over year. But Search advertising growth continued to decelerate, and Alphabet shares fell 8% following the results.

items.title: Creating AI value with enterprise context
items.summary: Across a business, any number of AI platforms, systems, and tools may be at work simultaneously—for example, AI-powered customer platforms, conversational assistants, and workflow and process automation tools. Each one is sophisticated, advanced, and quick to respond. But, when set to work, the outcomes and actions that emerge may be wrong, confused, or lacking a proper understanding of the business. Many organizations find themselves in this situation—and it could be one of key reasons they struggle to extract returns on their AI investments.

items.summary: If you ask some prominent US politicians who won the 2020 presidential election, you might get some weasely answers that fail to directly acknowledge Joe Biden's win that November. If you ask Google's AI Mode the same question, you might get an evasive answer that simply tells you to consult with outside sources. items.title: GitHub Expands Infra With 4 Mn Cores, Debuts Copilot Fusion for Multi-Model Routing
items.summary: After provisioning more than 3 million CPU cores and 120 petabytes of high-speed storage in August following a series of reliability incidents, GitHub is now doubling down on expanding its infrastructure by adding more than 4 million CPU cores and 160 PB of storage. This comes as GitHub experienced a massive surge in AI-driven commit activity recently, with 7.38 billion commits on GitHub in September alone—a 5x increase over the previous month. "Agents are changing the volume and shape of software development. Adding capacity matters, but capacity alone won’t get us there.

items.title: Otter adds ‘Work’ mode to automate more meeting-related tasks
items.summary: Otter has added a new Work mode to its AI Chat assistant, expanding the range of tasks it can carry out before and after meetings. It’s part of a wider drive by Otter — which received $320 million in funding last week — to move beyond meeting transcription and into automating tasks and workflows. The Work interface, announced Tuesday, is accessible in the AI Chat prompt box, alongside the Chat option. While Chat allows users to ask questions, generate content, and retrieve information, Work is aimed at multi-step actions, Otter said.

items.title: Gheist turns GitHub Actions into a secret extraction service
items.summary: A threat actor dubbed Gheist is turning compromised GitHub accounts into credential-harvesting platforms. By planting malicious GitHub Actions workflows in private repositories, attackers can expose repository and environment secrets, then retrieve them through GitHub APIs before deleting evidence of the activity. Tracked since September 15 by Wiz Research, the campaign has left more than 13,500 malicious branches across over 850 compromised accounts, spanning personal projects and private enterprise repositories. The campaign’s weapon is GitHub Actions , the platform’s automation service, which attackers are using to turn stolen access into harvested credentials.
